solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Destructive agent with strong desire to hold company back

indicators.note: the word for strong desire is said to hold the next piece, so it wraps around it

parts.note: lust is a strong desire

indicators.note: back tells us to read the abbreviation for company the other way round

explanation.surface: A wrecker driven by greed is holding a business back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destructive agent' sounds like a saboteur or a chemical, but it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarming locusts strip crops bare, a classic biblical plague and destroyer of harvests.

clue.text: Most fashionable office is in Paris

parts.note: lat is a short form of latrine, and office is an old euphemism for a lavatory
est is French for is

explanation.surface: The trendiest workplace is in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'office' (in the plural especially) was a polite British word for the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: The newest styles are the most up to date and so the trendiest.

clue.text: Larch growing wild round a standard thicket

indicators.note: the scrambled tree goes round the other pieces
wild suggests the tree's letters are disordered

parts.note: par is a standard or norm

explanation.surface: A larch tree growing wild in a dense patch of scrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing wild' rearranges LARCH, which splits as CH...RAL around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaparral is dense scrub of the American south-west, a type of thicket.

clue.text: Pay to remit including bonus

indicators.note: the verb for remitting includes the extra payment inside it

parts.note: to remit money is to send it
a tip is a bonus payment

explanation.surface: Wages are sent with a bonus added.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed regular salary, especially of a clergyman, is pay.

clue.text: Spot light of more than one colour

parts.note: a speck is a small spot
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a small light

explanation.surface: Seems to describe spotting a multicoloured light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something marked with flecks of a different shade shows more than one hue.

clue.text: Dock on isle and cross round base in carrier

parts.note: a port is a dock
the Isle of Man

indicators.note: the cross goes round the base letter

parts.note: a tau cross is T-shaped
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: Seems to describe loading a carrier at a dock on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A large travelling bag that opens into two halves carries clothes, so it is a carrier.

clue.text: Soldier perhaps entertained by jazz fan with a classical item

indicators.note: the insect is entertained, taken in, by the jazz enthusiast

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
a soldier is a kind of ant, so ant is given by example

explanation.surface: A soldier hosted by a jazz lover alongside a classical piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A choral work with solos and chorus, as by Bach, is a classical piece of music.

clue.text: Bob's losing head for old actress

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a bob, short for bobsleigh, is a sleigh

explanation.surface: A man called Bob is losing his hair, or head, for a veteran actress.
explanation.walkthrough: Vivien Leigh starred in Gone with the Wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivien Leigh was a star of the 1930s and 40s screen, an actress of a past era.

clue.text: Make devoted cadet die horribly

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters are badly mangled

explanation.surface: A trainee officer meets a grim end in the cause of loyalty.
explanation.definitionFit: To commit or give over wholly to a cause is to make someone devoted to it.

clue.text: Ending in rout such as Hamlet is upsetting

definitions.text: Ending in rout such as Hamlet is upsetting

indicators.note: the ending of the word rout means its final letter only
in a down-reading sense, upsetting turns the cigar brand over so it reads backwards

parts.note: Hamlet is a well-known British brand of small cigar

explanation.surface: A defeated army's end compared to the fate of Shakespeare's prince is distressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' does double duty: it turns CIGAR into RAGIC, and is the definition. Hamlet cigars were famous in the UK for TV adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: A play like Hamlet is a tragedy, and something deeply upsetting is described with the same adjective.

clue.text: Rampaging All Black that is tackled by Perry?

indicators.note: the rugby player and the abbreviation are held, as if tackled, by the tennis player's first name

parts.note: Fred Perry, the English tennis champion
an All Black is a New Zealand rugby player, NZ
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A wild New Zealand rugby player is brought down by someone named Perry.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampaging means acting in a wild, uncontrolled fury, the state of being berserk.

clue.text: Caught odd banger

parts.note: snared means caught in a trap
rum is an old-fashioned British word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Looks like someone caught eating a strange sausage, a banger being British slang for one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banger' suggests a sausage or an old car, but here it is something you bang in a drum kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum in a kit that is struck with sticks is literally a thing that is banged.

clue.text: You could get to bathe if you do this!

definitions.text: You could get to bathe if you do this!

parts.note: rock can signal a rearrangement, and the letters of the boat rocked give these two clue words

explanation.surface: Warning that disturbing the boat may land you in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, ROCK means 'shuffle' and THE BOAT shuffles to TO BATHE; literally, rock a boat and you may go overboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To cause trouble is the idiom's sense; literally, a rocking boat can tip you into the sea for a swim.

clue.text: Improvised revolutionary final passage around Beethoven's Fifth

indicators.note: around tells us the reversed musical term goes round the composer's letter
revolutionary means turning round, so the musical term is read backwards

parts.note: a coda is the final passage of a piece of music

indicators.note: the fifth of the composer's name means its fifth letter

explanation.surface: A musical piece improvised around Beethoven's Fifth Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' makes ADOC from CODA; 'around' puts it round H, the fifth letter of Beethoven.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done ad hoc is arranged for the moment without planning, which is to say made up on the spot.

clue.text: Chemical cutting down spy

parts.note: reducing means cutting down
an agent is a spy

explanation.surface: A spy is reducing their stock of a chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, a substance that donates electrons in a reaction is called by this name; it is a chemical.

clue.text: Cockney engaged originally in the role of nurse

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: as means in the role of
a tender is one who tends, as a nurse does

explanation.surface: A Londoner first engaged to play the part of a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockneys come from the East End of London, so a Cockney is a native of that district.

clue.text: Shoot to trap soldiers parking in armoured vehicle

indicators.note: the shoot traps the other pieces, wrapping round them

parts.note: a scion is a shoot or twig used in grafting
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: A shooter trapping troops who are parking in a tank.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scorpion was a British light tank, a type of armoured fighting vehicle.

clue.text: Everyone is immediately engrossed by leader of military's exercises

indicators.note: the earlier words are absorbed inside the abbreviation, so it wraps around them

parts.note: CIC is commander in chief, the leader of the military, plus the S of 's
all means everyone
then can mean at once, immediately after

explanation.surface: Everyone is suddenly absorbed in the commander's drill routines.
explanation.walkthrough: CIC (commander-in-chief) is the military's leader; the 's adds an S to it.
explanation.definitionFit: These are gymnastic drills done for fitness, so they are physical exercises.

clue.text: Wicked person whose memory will remain timeless

indicators.note: time is abbreviated T, and less means without, so that letter goes

parts.note: an immortal is someone whose memory will live on forever

explanation.surface: A villain whose memory will last forever, beyond time itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' tells you to take T (time) from IMMORTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked conduct is that which breaks moral codes, so is morally wrong.

clue.text: Angry compiler about to be outed in press

indicators.note: angry suggests the letters are stirred up and jumbled
to be outed means the abbreviation is thrown out of the word

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A cross setter about to be exposed in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C (circa) from COMPILER and shuffle OMPILER: 'Angry' is the anagram signal and 'to be outed' the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone is to urge or beg them earnestly.

clue.text: Robust analysis is about right

indicators.note: about means going round the abbreviation

parts.note: a study is an analysis

explanation.surface: A strong piece of research is broadly correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong and solidly built things are robust, firm and hard to break.

clue.text: Top European team with half leaving field

indicators.note: half of the club's name departs, so only the first half is kept

parts.note: Real Madrid, the leading Spanish football club

explanation.surface: A top football team leaves the field with half its players gone.
explanation.walkthrough: REAL MADRID has ten letters; keep the first five.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of study or activity is a domain or sphere, just as a kingdom is a territory.

clue.text: Small cake rising introducing fine TV programme that was popular once, briefly

definitions.text: TV programme that was popular once, briefly

indicators.note: the cake has the letter introduced into its middle
in a down clue rising means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a baba is a small rum-soaked sponge cake
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A little cake rising is bringing in a good old TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: AbFab is the short name of the 1990s BBC sitcom Absolutely Fabulous.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC sitcom Absolutely Fabulous was popular in the 1990s, and its nickname abbreviates it.

clue.text: Crack soldiers in alien kit

indicators.note: the joke and soldiers are placed in the alien, which surrounds them

parts.note: ET, the extra-terrestrial of the film
a crack is a witty remark, a quip
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Elite troops in strange gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Kit is the gear or apparatus needed for an activity, the same as the tools you carry.

clue.text: Presume European monarch will be overthrown as mediocre

parts.note: to infer is to presume or deduce

indicators.note: overthrown means turned upside down, so the French word is read backwards

parts.note: roi is French for king

explanation.surface: Someone assumes a weak European king will be deposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be overthrown' makes IOR from ROI, the French king.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-rate or of poor quality: something mediocre is lower in standard.

clue.text: It's for holding odd items from ledger

definitions.text: It's for holding odd items from ledger

indicators.note: the little word for holds the selected letters inside it
the odd-numbered letters of ledger are picked out, first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Describes a file for keeping stray papers taken from an accounts book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd items from' takes L, D, E from ledger; 'holding' puts them inside FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A binder or file is a container that keeps papers together, as the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Aristocrats showing complete lack of talent leaving area

parts.note: no means none at all, a complete lack

indicators.note: the abbreviation for area departs from the phrase

parts.note: ability is talent

explanation.surface: Suggests the upper classes reveal their utter incompetence by moving out of the district.
explanation.definitionFit: The titled class collectively, lords and ladies, are aristocrats.

clue.text: Sell singular radioactive emission, lacking heart

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: a beta ray is one stream of particles given off by radioactive material

explanation.surface: Someone peddles one heartless burst of radiation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking heart' removes the central A of BETARAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell someone out is to double-cross them, to be a traitor.
